content.text: {"primary_meaning":"God or Christ as the source of divine light, glory, righteousness, life, and healing—especially the traditional Christological image of the “sun of righteousness.”","primary_basis":["Malachi 4:2 — the “sun of righteousness” rises with healing; traditionally interpreted by Christians as referring to Christ.","Psalm 84:11 — “the LORD God is a sun and shield,” directly associating the sun with God’s beneficent presence.","Matthew 17:2 — at the Transfiguration, Christ’s face shines like the sun.","Revelation 1:16 — the glorified Christ’s face is like the sun shining at full strength.","Luke 1:78-79 — the dawn or dayspring from on high brings light to those in darkness, commonly read Christologically.","Isaiah 60:19-20 and Revelation 21:23 — God’s glory, and in Revelation the Lamb, supplies the ultimate light that surpasses the created sun."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"A ruler, patriarch, or supreme earthly authority.","basis":["Genesis 37:9-10 — Joseph’s sun, moon, and stars are interpreted within the narrative as his father, mother, and brothers.","The sun’s governance of the day in Genesis 1:16 has also supported broader ruler or governing-power symbolism."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The created cosmic order, whose darkening or disruption signifies divine judgment, catastrophe, or the end of the age.","basis":["Isaiah 13:10 — the darkened sun accompanies judgment on Babylon.","Joel 2:10,31 — the sun is darkened in connection with the day of the LORD.","Matthew 24:29; Mark 13:24; Luke 21:25 — solar darkening forms part of eschatological signs.","Revelation 6:12; 8:12; 9:2 — changes to the sun accompany apocalyptic judgment."],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"God’s universal providence and common blessing upon humanity.","basis":["Matthew 5:45 — God causes the sun to rise on both the evil and the good.","Psalm 19:4-6 — the sun’s course displays the ordered glory of creation."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"An object of forbidden pagan or idolatrous worship rather than a positive symbol.","basis":["Deuteronomy 4:19 and 17:3 — Israel is warned against worshiping the sun.","2 Kings 23:5,11 — solar worship is removed during Josiah’s reforms.","Ezekiel 8:16 — worship of the sun is depicted as an abomination."],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Divine splendor, heavenly investiture, or the glory surrounding the covenant people, especially in the woman “clothed with the sun.”","basis":["Revelation 12:1 — the woman clothed with the sun has been variously identified with Israel, the Church, Mary, or the people of God; the sun is commonly taken as heavenly or divine glory."],"prominence":"minority"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"medium","notes":"Christian tradition most recognizably uses the sun as an image of God or Christ’s radiant glory and righteousness, but Scripture assigns it different functions in different contexts. There is therefore no single settled symbolic meaning applicable to every occurrence."}
